newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania fund lures foreigners with sell-offs.
newsitem.headline: Romania fund lures foreigners with sell-offs.

text.p: Romania's main privatisation agency said on Friday it had drafted a list of 143 state companies on offer to foreign investors in a bid to step up sell-off of state companies and attract foreign investment.

"We offer stakes of 40 or 51 percent in profitable companies, as well as in firms which are less profitable, but operate in sectors with potential for growth," Viorel Ispas, spokesman for the State Ownership Fund (FPS) said.

The list includes refineries and petrochemical plants, aircraft and aircraft engine makers, car and railway carriage makers, ship builders, metallurgical and heavy machinery plants, furniture makers, and food and light industry plants.
The FPS said it would soon start work -- complete with documentation and offers -- to promote its sell-off programme.
The Fund, which has been handling Romanian privatisations since 1992, has been repeatedly accused of stalling sell-offs.

Late in 1995 it launched a mass sell-off offering Romanians up to 60 percent in 4,000 companies in a swap for coupons. In a separate scheme started in 1993, it privatised some 3,000 of the 6,500 companies in which it was a majority stockholder.
"The FPS list includes attractions and is varied, offering everything from an aircraft maker to a sewing thread plant. It is bound to appeal to foreigners," a local economist said.
Foreign investment in Romania is lower than elsewhere in Eastern Europe. Direct foreign capital injections since the 1989 fall of communism amounted to $2.1 billion at end-1996.

The coalition government which has been ruling Romania since last November's general polls has pledged to work out new laws and provide increased incentives to boost foreign investment levels in the Balkan country.
